paragraphs.en: In today's {mad} rush for success, many people believe that working to the maximum is the secret to success.Sometimes, taking breaks is seen as being {stupid} .Employees often find themselves working late into {midnight} hours, living in a {cruel} cycle without {liberty} to manage their personal time.However, life isn't about burning yourself out in pursuit of {wealth} or status.Research has found that moderation also gets results on the job.
paragraphs.cn: 在如今人们 <u> 疯狂 </u> 追求成功的浪潮中，许多人认为拼尽全力工作就是成功的秘诀。有时候，休息被视为 <u> 愚蠢 </u> 之举。员工经常发现自己工作到 <u> 午夜 </u> 时分，陷入一个 <u> 残酷 </u> 循环：他们没有支配个人时间的 <u> 自由 </u> 。然而，生活并非是要在追求 <u> 财富 </u> 或地位的过程中把自己累垮。研究发现，适度行事在工作中同样能取得成效。

paragraphs.en: In a study led by Ellen Langer of Harvard University, researchers asked people to {translate} sentences into a new {made-up} language.Subjects who practiced the language {moderately} {beforehand} made fewer {errors} than those who practiced {extensively} or not at all. {High} levels of knowledge can make people too {attached} to traditional ways of viewing problems in {domains} such as the arts, sciences, and {politics} .High {conscientiousness} creates an {emergency} state of constant productivity, which is related to lower job performance, especially in jobs where it doesn't {pay} to be a {perfectionist} , whether you're a {secretary} or a {police} {officer} .
paragraphs.cn: 在哈佛大学的艾伦·兰格主导的一项研究中，研究人员要求人们将句子 <u> 翻译 </u> 成一种 <u> 新造 </u> 的语言。与 <u> 大量 </u> 练习或完全不练习的人相比， <u> 事先适度地 </u> 练习这门语言的受试者出 <u> 错 </u> 更少。 <u> 高 </u> 水平的知识可能会让人们在艺术、科学、 <u> 政治 </u> 等 <u> 领域 </u> 看待问题时过分 <u> 喜欢 </u> 传统方式。高度的 <u> 尽责性 </u> 会造成一种始终保持高效产出的 <u> 紧急 </u> 状态，而这种状态与较低的工作表现相关，尤其是在那些做一个 <u> 完美主义者 </u> 并不会带来 <u> 收益 </u> 的工作中，无论你是一个 <u> 秘书 </u> 还是一名 <u> 警察 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: How long we stay on the clock and how we spend that time sitting on the {chair} are under careful examination in many workplaces.The young {bank} {clerk} who eats {lunch} at his desk is probably seen as a {go-getter} , while his {colleagues} who chat over a {relaxed} conference-room meal get dirty looks from the {corner} office.”People from cultures that value relationships more than {ours} does are {shocked} by the thought of eating alone in front of a computer,”says Art Markman, a professor at the University of Texas, Austin.The workplace is more than a place to earn a {wage} .Social interaction extends far beyond {committee} meetings.It has been shown to {lift} {mood} and get people thinking in new directions.The seemingly {innocent} exchanges such as sharing a {slice} of {pancake} or gathering for {lovely} conversations on {Friday} afternoon create invaluable connections that contribute to organizational success.
paragraphs.cn: 在许多工作场所，我们的工作时长，以及我们坐在 <u> 椅子 </u> 上的这段时间是如何度过的，都在受到仔细的审视。那位在办公桌前吃 <u> 午饭 </u> 的年轻 <u> 银行职员 </u> 很可能被视为一个 <u> 积极进取的人 </u> ，而他那些在会议室里 <u> 轻松 </u> 闲聊着用餐的 <u> 同事 </u> ，则会遭到办公室 <u> 角落 </u> 里领导的冷眼。得克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校教授阿特·马克曼说：”来自那些比 <u> 我们 </u> 更重视人际关系的文化背景的人们，一想到独自在电脑前吃饭就会感到 <u> 震惊 </u> 。”工作场所不仅仅是一个赚取 <u> 工资 </u> 的地方。社交互动远远超出了 <u> 委员 </u> 会议的范畴。事实证明，社交可以 <u> 提振情绪 </u> ，让人们从新的角度思考问题。像是分享一 <u> 片薄煎饼 </u> ，或是 <u> 周五 </u> 下午聚在一起 <u> 愉快地 </u> 聊天，这类看似 <u> 天真的 </u> 交流却能建立起宝贵的人际关系，而这些关系对机构的成功至关重要。

paragraphs.en: Markman also promotes off-task time.”Part of being a good thinker is experiencing things that are {seemingly} {unrelated} to what you are working on at the moment but give you fresh ideas about your work,”he says.”Also, there is a lot of research showing that a positive mood leads to higher levels of {productivity} and creativity.So, when people do things to increase their life {satisfaction} , they also make themselves more effective at work.”
paragraphs.cn: 马克曼还提倡安排一些不处理工作任务的时间。他说：”成为一个善于思考的人，就要体验一些 <u> 看似 </u> 与目前的工作 <u> 无关 </u> 却能给你的工作带来新思路的事情。此外，大量研究表明，积极的情绪会带来更高的 <u> 生产力 </u> 和创造力。因此，当人们做一些提高生活 <u> 满意度 </u> 的事时，他们也让自己的工作效率变得更高了。” 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
